sources.cite: Microsoft Learn, Blob rehydration from the archive tier
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: rehydrate by copying to an online tier (the source stays in archive, no early deletion fee) or by Set Blob Tier; standard priority 'might take up to 15 hours to complete for objects under 10 GB', high priority 'might complete in less than one hour for objects under 10 GB' (costs more, for emergencies); a pending standard request can be raised to high; archive blobs should stay 180 days or pay early deletion; a 10 GiB per hour per account rehydration limit. Sharing with a time-limited SAS and container public access are from memory of the Blob storage security pages (to verify).

brief.situation: You are a data analyst at Corvin Garden Supply. The external auditor needs 120 supplier invoices from 2024 (PDFs, 1.8 GB in total) by 15:00 today, or the audit finding escalates to the board. The invoices are in the storage account cgsdocs, container invoices, which a lifecycle rule moved to the Archive tier after 180 days.
handover: The auditor can download from a link you send; they have no account in your tenant.
Company policy: invoices are confidential; no public access on any container.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the archived invoices, the online copy you make and how the auditor gets them.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: The auditor needs the files by 15:00, 150 minutes after the request; high priority rehydration can finish in under an hour for small objects, standard can take up to 15 hours.

writeup.question: For the record: why the invoices could not be downloaded, how you got them out in time, and how you shared them.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: A lifecycle rule moved the 2024 invoices to Archive after 180 days; archived blobs are offline and must be rehydrated before they can be read.

parts.label: In time
parts.modelAnswer: Copied the 120 invoices (1.8 GB, each small) to a Hot container with high priority, which can finish in under an hour; standard priority can take up to 15 hours. Copying left the archived originals untouched.

parts.label: Shared
parts.modelAnswer: A read-only SAS on the audit container, HTTPS only, for seven days, and the container deleted after the audit. Making the invoices container public would have exposed everything.

publicContainer.headline: Access and tier are different problems
publicContainer.body: The files were offline because of their tier, not their permissions. Rehydrate a copy, then share only those files with a time-limited SAS.

auditEscalated.headline: Archive is offline storage
auditEscalated.body: Archived blobs cannot be read until rehydrated. For an urgent need on small objects, use high priority; standard can take up to 15 hours.

delivered.headline: Good: knew the tiers
delivered.body: You saw the files were archived and small, copied just those at high priority instead of waiting on standard, checked them, and shared them narrowly with an expiry.

scoring.modelReasoning: The invoices are in the Archive tier, which is offline; they need rehydrating, and they are small. Copy just the 120 to a new Hot container with high priority, which can finish in under an hour, leaving the originals archived. Standard priority can take up to 15 hours. Share the copies with a read-only, expiring SAS; making the container public would expose every invoice and would not even bring the archived files back.
